text: I come here often for coffee on my way to work. The service is fast and efficient, and the employees are mostly friendly even though it looks frantically busy back there! However, this morning I saw the most awful display by someone I can only assume is a manager. In Vancouver, a city with a higher than average street homeless population and currently facing a massive public health emergency that is especially affecting these marginalized people, this manager bullied and condescended to a homeless man in a way that was absolutely shocking. After speaking loudly right at the man and actually getting an answer, he decided to speak over his head to the employees, who were also visibly embarrassed at his actions. "Did he buy something?", he asked. When told that yes, he had ordered a coffee just like hundreds of other people that morning, he continued: "Okay well can we get it so that I can get him out of here?". I had no words at the time for how shocked and disappointed I am. For someone in a leadership position and working for a company that claims to take its role in the community so seriously, this was an unbelievable lack of compassion. And not that this even matters, but the homeless man in question had been quiet, polite, and not bothering or even speaking to any other customers or staff. I'm still shaking my head about this.
author: Stephanie Plourde

text:
The staff does not wear gloves whole preparing food. And when asked why, they said Mcd only has a policy of washing hands before handling food and gloves are not allowed.
Under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations (SFCR) food workers in all kinds of food industry should not only wash hands but also wear Clear/white gloves for assembling or handling ready to eat food along with other extra protective coverings. How would I know the person who is making food is not touching the dirty parts of the counter. In between making the breakfast wraps, the staff touched many other parts, left the station, touched non food surfaces which I can assure are not cleaned or changed at proper interval of time.
I work in healthcare and I know that even after handwashing, there are still bacteria that remain on skin. Handwashing reduces viruses, but does not remove or kill them all. Even clean hands can contaminate food if the worker has Cuts, Dry skin, Wounds, Fingernail bacteria.
What would happen in busy hours of the day, if they can forget to put my customized items in the wrap then they can obviously prevent hand washing to handle the food orders during busy time. This is really unhygienic way of preparing food. And if really Mcd has a policy of not wearing gloves then it should definitely be implemented.
author: Kashish Kumar

text:
Extremely Disappointed — Still No Refund After 4 Months

I placed an order through your app the day before my visit. However, when I arrived at the store, the app completely crashed and said the order could not be retrieved. Left with no choice, I placed a second order in-store and paid again.

Since then, I have contacted your team multiple times requesting a refund for the original order that I never received. The manager promised the refund would be issued, but here we are — four months later, and nothing has happened. No update, no refund, no responsibility taken.

This level of disorganization and poor customer service is beyond frustrating. It’s just $9.96, but the principle matters. Since you clearly don’t care, consider it a donation — may it bring you some good karma, and hopefully, some common sense.

Absolutely unacceptable.
author: Ron Hu

On top of that, they also state they are open 24 hours, yet they shut their indoor dining down at 6pm most days and only allow mobile ordering which is extremely frustrating if someone wants to use cash or for elderly people who are not as experienced in technology but would still like something to eat.

Overall, no matter how desperate you get, go elsewhere. You won’t regret not spending your money here.
